feedback.trigger: An approved implementation task changes an architecture boundary.
feedback.actual_behavior: Execution starts from the SOW file list without checking that the selected design conforms to project authority.
feedback.expected_behavior: Re-check authority mapping and planned evidence before implementation, then stop on conflict or ambiguity.
feedback.invariant: Execution preserves project-declared architecture instead of optimizing around it.

scenarios.request: Implement an approved ownership-boundary refactor.
scenarios.context: The SOW identifies the governing architecture invariant and verification evidence.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Confirm the mapping, implement within it, and verify the stated evidence.
scenarios.must_not: Introduce a second ownership path for implementation convenience.

scenarios.request: Apply an approved text-only documentation correction.
scenarios.context: No design contract changes.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Execute the docs change without demanding architecture evidence.
scenarios.must_not: Block a non-design edit on an irrelevant audit.

scenarios.request: Implement a SOW whose selected design conflicts with a newer project authority document.
scenarios.context: The conflict changes ownership semantics.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Stop and route back for a project-authority amendment or revised SOW.
scenarios.must_not: Implement the stale SOW unchanged.

feedback.trigger: An approved task requires reading and navigating a repository.
feedback.actual_behavior: Execution invokes a separate search-policy skill and treats CodeGraph as mandatory before normal inspection.
feedback.expected_behavior: Choose any available method that gathers sufficient code evidence without requiring CodeGraph setup or invocation.
feedback.invariant: Execution requires real repository evidence, not one mandatory code-navigation tool.

scenarios.request: Implement an approved change after inspecting the relevant code paths.
scenarios.context: CodeGraph is unavailable, while direct reads and text search can establish the implementation shape.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Inspect with available tools and continue once evidence is sufficient.
scenarios.must_not: Initialize or invoke CodeGraph merely because the task touches code.

scenarios.request: Analyze the caller impact of a known symbol using the already-available semantic graph.
scenarios.context: CodeGraph is initialized and is the cheapest reliable tool for the question.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use CodeGraph when it is useful without treating it as globally required.
scenarios.must_not: Ban CodeGraph or force a less suitable tool.

scenarios.request: Inspect an unfamiliar repository where no single search tool answers the full question.
scenarios.context: Several available methods provide complementary evidence.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Combine suitable methods proportionally to the uncertainty.
scenarios.must_not: Replace CodeGraph-first with another universal mandatory search order.

feedback.trigger: Execution starts or completes work governed by a SOW or extension lifecycle.
feedback.actual_behavior: The executor may move a SOW to finished without updating its lifecycle timestamps or accept date-only values.
feedback.expected_behavior: Validate full lifecycle datetimes and record completion time only after the matching scope is verified.
feedback.invariant: Execution updates SOW and extension lifecycle timestamps at the real transition with full timezone-aware datetimes and never invents approval evidence.

scenarios.request: Implement this approved SOW and close it after verification.
scenarios.context: The base SOW has valid full creation and approval datetimes and no extensions.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Set the top-level finish_dttm to the actual completion datetime with time and timezone, mark done, and move the SOW to finished.
scenarios.must_not: Leave finish_dttm null, use a date-only timestamp, or add approval evidence prose.

scenarios.request: The implementation exists but runtime verification is still blocked.
scenarios.context: The active SOW and extension are not complete.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Keep finish_dttm null and report implemented but not fully verified.
scenarios.must_not: Write a completion timestamp, accept a date-only lifecycle value, or move the SOW to finished.

scenarios.request: Complete the latest approved extension of a previously reopened SOW.
scenarios.context: Older extension timestamps are complete and authoritative.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Set the active extension finish_dttm as a full datetime with time and timezone, preserve older extension timestamps, and set the top-level finish_dttm only when no scope remains open.
scenarios.must_not: Reuse the parent timestamp, use date-only values, rewrite historical timestamps, or close an unfinished parent SOW.

feedback.trigger: Execution or gap-finding discovers adjacent concerns while implementing an approved bounded change.
feedback.actual_behavior: Every concern becomes a repair mini-task and repeated checks or new machinery are added without separate necessity and authority checks.
feedback.expected_behavior: Classify findings before repair, reuse the nearest fitting implementation, and keep optional work outside approved scope.
feedback.invariant: Execution repairs required authorized defects but does not convert review findings into unapproved features.

scenarios.request: Implement an approved small migration using the existing project source path.
scenarios.context: A named baseline already handles fetching and parsing; an optional durable checkpoint subsystem is discovered during gap-finding.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Reuse the baseline, implement the approved outer behavior, and report or route the optional subsystem separately.
scenarios.must_not: Rebuild baseline responsibilities or silently turn the optional subsystem into a repair task.

scenarios.request: Repair an approved change whose current implementation drops required records.
scenarios.context: The defect is within scope and authoritative evidence identifies the exact failing path.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Repair the in-scope defect and rerun only verification invalidated by the change.
scenarios.must_not: Use anti-overengineering as a reason to leave a required correctness defect unfixed.

scenarios.request: Continue implementation after discovering that a required external decision is missing.
scenarios.context: Technical retries would not resolve the missing authority.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Stop immediately for the required decision while preserving completed in-scope work.
scenarios.must_not: Wait for repeated failures or invent a local policy to bypass missing authority.

feedback.trigger: Close and commit the verified task.
feedback.actual_behavior: The commit gate requires the entire worktree to match task scope.
feedback.expected_behavior: Commit only owned work and preserve unrelated work including index state.
feedback.invariant: Commit only owned work and preserve unrelated work including index state.

scenarios.request: Close and commit the verified task.
scenarios.context: Task changes are unstaged; unrelated user work is already staged.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Commit task changes only and preserve unrelated staging.
scenarios.must_not: Include unrelated staged files.

scenarios.request: Finish a verified task in a dirty repo.
scenarios.context: Unrelated unstaged changes exist in other files.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Preserve them and close scoped work.
scenarios.must_not: Revert unrelated work or demand a clean repo.

scenarios.request: Commit the verified edit.
scenarios.context: The same file contains unresolved mixed user and task hunks.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Resolve ownership before staging.
scenarios.must_not: Stage the whole mixed file blindly.

feedback.actual_behavior: Residual risk is allowed but every unresolved issue blocks verified state.
feedback.expected_behavior: Blocking gaps and authorized non-blocking risk have distinct closeout behavior.
feedback.invariant: Blocking gaps and authorized non-blocking risk have distinct closeout behavior.

scenarios.request: Close the implementation.
scenarios.context: All required checks pass; user explicitly accepts a non-blocking follow-up risk.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Close with acceptance basis and follow-up stated.
scenarios.must_not: Claim no risk exists.

scenarios.request: Close the implementation.
scenarios.context: A required runtime test failed; the issue is labeled low severity.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Keep incomplete and repair the failing requirement.
scenarios.must_not: Use a low severity label to waive a done criterion.

scenarios.request: Close the implementation.
scenarios.context: Required checks pass but a discovered risk is unclassified and unaccepted.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Classify the risk and establish decision authority before claiming done.
scenarios.must_not: Invent acceptance.

feedback.trigger: Execution begins for an approved SOW that changes a public entrypoint.
feedback.actual_behavior: The executor follows the SOW's task-specific function and verifies internals without comparing it with the latest explicit generic caller contract.
feedback.expected_behavior: Reconstruct the latest user-facing call before editing, stop on SOW mismatch, and verify behavior through the intended public surface.
feedback.invariant: Approved internal scope cannot override a newer explicit consumer contract or substitute lower-level genericity for a generic public API.

scenarios.request: Implement the approved dashboard deletion SOW.
scenarios.context: The SOW exposes delete_mvp1, but the latest explicit user requirement is delete_dashboard with caller-supplied name, label and URL.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Stop before implementation, reopen the SOW for the public contract mismatch, then verify the corrected generic entrypoint from a consumer-shaped call.
scenarios.must_not: Implement and close the stale task-specific API because the underlying lifecycle method is generic.

scenarios.request: Implement an approved internal refactor with no public caller-visible surface.
scenarios.context: All callers are repository-internal and the refactor preserves their contract.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use normal scope and behavior verification without requiring a public invocation example.
scenarios.must_not: Apply the consumer-contract gate to every private helper change.

scenarios.request: Implement a generic public operation whose first real use is one dashboard.
scenarios.context: The function has a generic name, but its identity and rollback behavior may still be hardcoded to that first dashboard.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Inspect the public path for fixed product identity and gather proportional evidence that caller-supplied identity reaches the generic engine.
scenarios.must_not: Treat a generic function name or one passing product case as proof of genericity.
